title: My Steam game's demo is live | Zone Idle
author: _Dickie_
selftext:
I've been building Zone Idle, an idle extraction game, mostly by directing Claude Code. The free demo just went live on Steam, so here's what that actually looked like.



[Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4330500/Zone_Idle/)

[Trailer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bGKoBB-fVUA)



How I work with it



\- I'm the designer, tester and editor. I decide what goes in, play every change, and push back when something feels off. Claude writes most of the code.

\- Bigger features start as a written spec and a step by step plan before any code gets written. That habit saved me from a lot of half-finished rewrites.

\- Tests first. A bug fix starts with a test that fails, then the fix. With 4,000+ tests, a change on one side of the game can't quietly break the other side.



What was hard



\- The grid inventory. Dragging items across nested containers made things duplicate or disappear more than once. The notes file has a whole section on it now, plus a stress test suite that hammers it.

\- It will confidently tell you something works. You still have to play it. Some of the best fixes came from me watching it in game and saying "this looks wrong".

\- Porting to Steam (Electron, Steam Cloud saves, achievements, a separate demo build) was a project of its own.



Also made with AI help



\- The item icons were generated by Gemini, reviewed and cleaned up by me

\- The trailer. I recorded the clips, and Claude wrote the scripts that cut them to the music's beat and typed out the captions



The game's soundtrack is a licensed music pack i purchased, and the trailer track is CC0.



If you try the demo, I'd love to hear what you think.
